meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Takes a long -uu-/-oo- stem with possessive endings in Jordanian (أخوي my brother, أخوك your brother); dual أخوين.

examples.trans: My older brother lives in Amman.
The brothers sat together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زرقا, plural: زرق).

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Primary colour adjective ('black'); feminine and non-human plural form is سودا (sooda).

examples.text: جيب لفة لزاق أسود من الدكان.
examples.trans: Pick up a roll of black tape from the shop.
The black cat is sleeping under the tree.

meanings.note: Warm greeting used alone (أهلا!), with فيك/فيكي ('welcome to you!'), or paired as أهلا وسهلا! ('you are most welcome!').

examples.trans: Hello, I am Tariq!
Welcome to Jasmine House!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أباريق.

examples.trans: The teapot is hot on the table.
Pour the hot water into the teapot.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian for 12. From eleven up, the counted noun stays singular: اتنعش فنجان 'twelve cups'.

examples.trans: We have twelve guests tonight.
It's twelve noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتري, بيشتري).

examples.trans: Tell me exactly what to buy.
Buy both brass valves together.

meanings.note: Form VII Medio-passive of دفع ('to pay'): اندفع حقه means 'its price has been paid'.

examples.trans: The bill was paid in cash at the desk.
Everything was paid for at the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنكسر, بينكسر).

examples.trans: The brass pressure valve broke.
Not a single glass broke in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Form VII passive of لف ('to wrap, turn'), common for parcels and fragile dishes.

examples.trans: The cups were wrapped well in newspaper.

examples.text: الخبز السخن ما بينلف بكيس مسكر.
examples.trans: Hot bread is not wrapped in a closed bag.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببرد, بيبرد).

examples.trans: The cake is cooling on the rack right now.
The radiator is starting to get cold at the bottom.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيانوهات.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Everyday word for a newspaper; broken plural in spoken Levantine is جرايد (jaraayid).

examples.text: عمي بيقرا الجريدة مع فنجان قهوة كل صبح.
examples.trans: My uncle reads the newspaper with a cup of coffee every morning.

examples.text: لف البياع الصحون بورق جرايد قديم.
examples.trans: The seller wrapped the plates in old newspaper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجرب, بيجرب).

examples.trans: This sweater is clean and new — try it on.
We tried the new recipe and it turned out delicious.

meanings.note: Before a noun or clause حتى means 'even' (حتى والغرفة فاضية 'even when the room is empty').

examples.text: حتى والغرفة فاضية، السلك بيرن مرتين.
examples.trans: Even when the room is empty, the wire rings twice.
Even room four's bell went quiet!

meanings.note: From ح-ر-ر ('hot, warm'); describes warmth retained by clay cups or weather temperature.

examples.text: الفخار السميك بيحفظ حرارة الشاي وقت طويل.
examples.trans: Thick pottery holds the heat of the tea for a long time.
The oven temperature is ideal for morning bread.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحط, بيحط).

examples.trans: Where should I put the spoons and napkins?
I put the suitcase beside the table.

meanings.note: Used in معك حق ('you are right / you have a point').

examples.trans: You are right, the weather is cold today.
Everyone has a right to rest.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حلوة, plural: حلوين).

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I would like coffee with hot milk.
We bought three bottles of milk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحمل, بيحمل).

examples.text: بتحمل مفك بكل مكان يا طارق!
examples.trans: You carry a screwdriver everywhere, Tariq!
He picked up the wrong blue bag at the station.

حِفِظ.gloss: to keep safe; hold onto; preserve

meanings.en: to keep safe; hold onto; preserve
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحفظ, بيحفظ).

examples.trans: Old stone holds the warmth until morning.

examples.text: شكرا لأنك حفظت الشنتة طول الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Thank you for keeping the bag safe all week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خصومات.

examples.trans: We gave him a fifty-percent discount.
There is a special discount for weekly guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine market word (from Italian dozzina) for a set of twelve; dual دزينتين ('two dozen' = 24).

examples.trans: We bought a dozen white cups for the café.

examples.text: الدكان بيعمل خصم إذا أخدت دزينتين.
examples.trans: The shop gives a discount if you take two dozen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: رفوف.

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
There are two pieces left on the shelf.

meanings.note: Opposite of سميك ('thick'); describes thin glass cups, fine lines, or narrow strips.

examples.text: كاسات القزاز الرفيعة حلوة للشاي بالنعنع.
examples.trans: Thin glass cups are lovely for mint tea.

examples.text: رسم رامي خط رفيع بقلم الرصاص.
examples.trans: Rami drew a fine line in pencil.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رنات.

examples.trans: The doorbell gave a single ring.
I heard two quick rings from the buzzer.

meanings.note: Standard Jordanian/Levantine household word for a ceramic or glass soup/breakfast bowl (plural زبادي).

examples.text: حطت سلمى الزيتون بزبدية فخار بيضا.
examples.trans: Salma put the olives in a white ceramic bowl.

examples.text: ع الطاولة أربع زبادي صغار للمربى.
examples.trans: On the table sit four small bowls for jam.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سميكة, plural: سماك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف السميك هون؟
examples.trans: Who left this thick envelope here?
Thick stone walls hold the warmth.

meanings.note: Abstract noun from سهل ('easy'); بسهولة means 'easily, with ease'.

examples.trans: The new key turns in the lock easily.

examples.text: كل كرسي بيطوي بسهولة بكبسة وحدة.
examples.trans: Every chair folds easily with a single press.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'together'.

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
We drank morning coffee together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: With pronoun suffixes in Jordanian, شكلك / شكلها often means 'you look / it looks' (شكلها حلوة it looks lovely).

examples.trans: How does the new tie look today?
The cake looks delicious!

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Everyday word for both a dinner plate and a teacup saucer (صحن الفنجان).

examples.text: رتبت سلمى اتنعش صحن أبيض جنب الفناجين.
examples.trans: Salma arranged twelve white saucers next to the cups.

examples.text: حطي الكيك السخن بصحن كبير عالطاولة.
examples.trans: Put the warm cake on a big plate on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصوات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of rain on the window.
His voice is calm and polite on the phone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for blackboard/signboard chalk (single stick: حبة طباشير).

examples.text: كتب البياع الأسعار بالطباشير الأبيض عاللوحة.
examples.trans: The vendor wrote the prices in white chalk on the board.

examples.text: امسحي لوحة الطباشير واكتبي قائمة اليوم.
examples.trans: Wipe the chalkboard and write today's menu.

meanings.note: Used in عالطريق ('on the way') and طول الطريق ('all the way').

examples.trans: The hot tea is on the way right now!
I repeated the sentence all along the way.

meanings.note: Before a time noun, طول (tuul) means 'all ... long / throughout' (طول الليل all night long, طول الأسبوع all week).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طويلة, plural: طوال).

examples.text: في رجال طويل واقف عند البوابة.
examples.trans: There is a tall man standing by the gate.
Three years was a long time.

meanings.note: Material noun naming potter's clay (طين الفخار) as well as wet earth after rain.

examples.text: فناجين الطين السميك بتخلي الشاي سخن.
examples.trans: Thick clay cups keep the tea hot.

examples.text: ريحة الطين بعد المطر بتنعش الحارة كلها.
examples.trans: The scent of earth after rain refreshes the whole neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.
Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: Numeral 'ten'; short form عشر ('ashar) before a plural noun (عشر دقايق 'ten minutes').

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Handcrafted fired clay vessels and cups, a staple of Jordanian and Levantine street markets.

examples.text: اشترينا إبريق وفناجين من بسطة الفخار.
examples.trans: We bought a pitcher and cups from the pottery stall.

examples.text: المي ببريق الفخار بتضل باردة بالصيف.
examples.trans: Water in a clay pitcher stays cool in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفكر, بيفكر).

examples.trans: I thought it was lost when we sold the house!
We thought the matter through calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فناجين.

examples.trans: I set two teacups on the tray.
This is my favourite coffee cup.

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of زجاج ('glass').

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كاسات.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
He poured half a glass of orange juice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كاملة, plural: كاملين).

examples.trans: He hired her for a full-time job at the guesthouse.
They stayed with us a full week.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word (lazzaaq) for sticky tape or electrical tape (لزاق كهربا).

examples.text: لف طارق السلك الجديد بلزاق كهربا أسود.
examples.trans: Tariq wrapped the new wire with black electrical tape.

examples.text: عندك لفة لزاق بالمكتب يا نور؟
examples.trans: Do you have a roll of tape at the desk, Nour?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلف, بيلف).

examples.text: لفي شمال برا البوابة وامشي دغري.
examples.trans: Turn left outside the gate and walk straight.
Turn left at the stair landing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian conjunction 'when' (in statements, not questions).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لوحات.

examples.text: شوف لوحة المفاتيح الخشب ورا المكتب.
examples.trans: Look at the wooden key board behind the desk.
We wiped the dust off the brass plate.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مدورة, plural: مدورين).

examples.trans: Where should I hang the round mirror?
We put a round wooden table in the corner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسك, بيمسك).

examples.trans: Hold this torch steady right here.
Grab the boxes, Tariq!

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مهندسين.

examples.trans: His brother is a skilled architect in Amman.
The engineer inspected the walls of the old building.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'one hundred' (مية مرة 'a hundred times' — construct مية miyyet before a noun).

examples.trans: Yes, a hundred times yes!
I am one hundred percent sure.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنسى, بينسى).

examples.trans: You forgot the notebook beside the soup bowl.
With all the rush, I completely forgot!

meanings.note: Unvocalised نفس covers nafas ('breath': خد نفس عميق take a deep breath) and nafs ('same': نفس الشي the same thing).

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

meanings.note: Masculine هادي ('quiet') is homographic with the feminine demonstrative هادي ('this'); context and agreement distinguish them cleanly.

examples.trans: The spot above the tree is very quiet.
We prepared the quiet attic room for you.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'he' or 'it' (masculine).

examples.trans: He knows heritage law well.

examples.text: بيحكي هيك وهو بيطل من الشباك!
examples.trans: He says that while peeking out the window!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of وراء ('behind, past').

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Collective ورق ('paper / tree leaves'), singulative ورقة ('a sheet of paper / note'), plural أوراق ('documents / papers').

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: For door handles and bag handles, Jordanian speakers often say يد الباب / عاليد alongside إيد for the human hand.

examples.text: ارفعي يد الباب أول وبعدين ادفعي.
examples.trans: Lift the door handle first, then push.

examples.text: في بطاقة مربوطة على يد الشنتة.
examples.trans: There is a tag tied to the handle of the bag.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational bridge introducing an inference ('so that means...'), clarification, or gentle pause ('I mean...').

examples.trans: So the house says hello by itself?
Does that mean there is no heating tonight?
